items.title: Clinical trial of a prion disease drug candidate begins enrolling participants
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.broadinstitute.org/news/clinical-trial-prion-disease-drug-candidate-begins-enrolling-participants Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50028027 Points: 28 # Comments: 2
items.content:
It’s the first time the potential treatment, a small interfering RNA targeting the prion protein, is being tested in humans.

A new drug candidate designed to slow the progression of prion disease is entering a phase 1 clinical trial , which will evaluate the potential medicine for safety and tolerability.

Prion diseases are a class of neurodegenerative disorders that are caused by the accumulation of misfolded prion protein (PrP) in the brain. There are currently no cures, and the disease is fatal within months or years after symptoms begin. The new drug candidate, developed by Broad Institute and University of Massachusetts Chan Medical School scientists, is a small interfering RNA (siRNA) that binds and snips RNA molecules encoding the prion protein, reducing the amount of the disease-causing protein in the brain. Previous research in animals has shown that lowering prion protein levels can delay onset and slow down the disease. The trial, called PrP-targeting siRNA Safety & Mechanism Study (PRiSM), is enrolling patients exhibiting symptoms of the disease.

“To finally advance this drug to a human trial is the long-overdue achievement of a longstanding dream, but it's also the very beginning of learning about this drug's safety and activity in humans,” said Eric Minikel , principal investigator of the trial and codirector of Broad’s Prion Therapeutic Science program. “I am looking forward to finding out whether this candidate has a future as a drug in our disease, but no matter what the outcome, as sponsor-investigators, we will learn a lot about how to run a clinical trial in prion disease, and we plan to broadly and publicly share our data and findings to benefit all sponsors who want to develop drugs for prion disease.”

The drug candidate is a divalent siRNA: two identical siRNAs that are linked together and designed to distribute more broadly in the brain than single siRNAs. The divalent siRNA was developed at the UMass Chan Medical School by Anastasia Khvorova and her lab. Khvorova, Minikel, and Sonia Vallabh , codirector of Broad’s Prion Therapeutic Science program, have been working together since 2019 on developing an siRNA-based drug to target prion protein mRNA. Vallabh and Minikel, who are wife and husband, have dedicated their lives to creating a cure or treatment for prion disease, after learning in 2011 that Vallabh has the genetic mutation that causes the disease.

In March 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared the team’s Investigational New Drug (IND) application to start a clinical trial on this drug candidate — a document that is usually kept private by drug companies. However, Minikel and Vallabh published their IND filing publicly, and have committed to sharing new insights openly.

This green light from the FDA — a significant step in the drug development process — follows promising animal data from the Minikel/Vallabh lab. The scientists showed that a divalent siRNA lowered prion protein in mice by 49 percent and resulted in a 64 percent increase in survival time with a single dose after symptom onset. The study is published in Nucleic Acids Research .

The clinical trial is being supported by NeuroNEXT, or Network for Excellence in Neuroscience Clinical Trials, a program of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), a part of the National Institutes of Health. NeuroNEXT provides both funding as well as infrastructure to run the trial, including trial sites, a clinical coordinating center housed at Mass General Hospital’s Neurology Department, and a data and statistics center at the University of Iowa.

“Eric and Sonia are visionaries who are not only top-notch scientists, but have enormous ethical conviction. I’m honored to have an opportunity to work with them,” said Khvorova, professor in UMass’s RNA Therapeutics Institute and Program in Molecular Medicine. “Their commitment to transparency is paving a new path for running a clinical trial, so we’re not only advancing therapy for prion disease, it’s advancing the field as a whole.”

The initial phase of the trial will enroll 15 symptomatic patients who will each receive one dose of the siRNA by lumbar puncture, and new patients enrolled over the course of the trial will receive larger doses than patients enrolled earlier. The trial will also have an observational arm consisting of 15 additional participants who will not receive any treatment. Minikel says they hope to add pre-sympomatic participants in the future. They also plan to share safety data as soon as they are able.

“Standard drug development is, for all sorts of reasons, not well set up to be a learning system,” Vallabh said. “But we can’t afford to treat each shot on goal as a self-contained unit – everything needs to feed the mission. I wish the absolute best for this exact molecule, and I also know that however it performs in the clinic, this experience must move us forward. It’s our job to figure out how.”

This is now the second clinical trial that Vallabh and her team at Broad have helped to enable. The first one, initiated by Ionis Pharmaceuticals, began in 2023 for drug candidate ION717 and is ongoing. In their lab, Minikel and Vallabh are pursuing other possible therapeutic approaches for prion disease, including epigenetic and gene editing .

To learn more about PRiSM, visit ClinicalTrials.gov and CureFFI.org , where Minikel shares information for the prion patient and scientific communities. For patient resources, Minikel and Vallabh recommend visiting the CJD Foundation .

The drug development was funded by National Institutes of Health grants and by donations from members of the prion disease community to the Broad Institute and to Prion Alliance . This clinical trial is being funded by the National Institutes of Neurological Disorders and Stroke through the NeuroNEXT program (Grant 3OT2NS138339-01S2).

Gentile J, et al. Divalent siRNA for prion disease . Nucleic Acids Research . Online April 24, 2026. DOI: 10.1093/nar/gkag287

items.title: Compiling Rust to readable C with Eurydice
items.summary: Article URL: https://lwn.net/Articles/1055211/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027853 Points: 46 # Comments: 5
items.content:
A few years ago, the only way to compile Rust code was using the rustc compiler with LLVM as a backend. Since then, several projects, including Mutabah's Rust Compiler (mrustc), GCC's Rust support (gccrs), rust_codegen_gcc , and Cranelift have made enormous progress on diversifying Rust's compiler implementations. The most recent such project, Eurydice , has a more ambitious goal: converting Rust code to clean C code. This is especially useful in high-assurance software, where existing verification and compliance tools expect C. Until such tools can be updated to work with Rust, Eurydice could provide a smoother transition for these projects, as well as a stepping-stone for environments that have a C compiler but no working Rust compiler. Eurydice has been used to compile some post-quantum-cryptography routines from Rust to C, for example.

Eurydice was started in 2023, and includes some code under the MIT license and some under the Apache-2.0 license. It's part of the Aeneas project, which works to develop several different tools related to applying formal verification tools to Rust code. The various Aeneas projects are maintained by a group of people employed by Inria (France's national computer-science-research institution) and Microsoft, but they do accept outside contributions.

Eurydice follows the same general structure as many compilers: take a Rust program, convert it into an intermediate representation (IR), modify the IR with a series of passes, and then output it as code in a lower-level language (in this case, C). Jonathan Protzenko, the most prolific contributor to Eurydice, has a blog post where he explains the project's approach. Unlike other compilers, however, Eurydice is concerned with preserving the overall structure of the code while removing constructs that exist in Rust but not in C. For example, consider this Rust function that calculates the least common multiple of two numbers using their greatest common denominator:

Whether this C code counts as "readable" is probably a matter of individual taste. It does, however, preserve the structure of the code. Even the evaluation order of the original is preserved by adding extra temporary variables ( uu____0 in example_lcm() ) where necessary to define an order. (Rust guarantees that if the multiplication overflows and causes a panic, that will happen before any side effects caused by calling example_gcd() , but C only guarantees that if the multiplication is performed in a separate statement.) Compiling the same functions with rustc results in a pair of entangled loops filled with bit-twiddling operations, instead — which is appropriate for machine-code output, but much less readable.

Of course, not all Rust programs can be faithfully represented in C. For example, for loops that use an iterator instead of a range need to be compiled to while loops that call into some of Eurydice's support code to manage the state of the iterator. More importantly, C has no concept of generics, so Rust code needs to be monomorphized during conversion. This can result in several different implementations of a function that differ only by type — often, the more idiomatic C approach would be to use macros or void * arguments.

The implementation of dynamically sized types also poses certain challenges. In Rust, a structure can be defined where one of its fields does not have a fixed size — like flexible array members in C:

But if that structure is generic, and one of the generic users of the type gives the flexibly sized field a type with a known size, the compiler can take advantage of that knowledge to elide bounds checks where appropriate.

This kind of separation, where some parts of the code may know the size of a type and some may not, is an important semantic detail to preserve in C because of how it interacts with the possibility of formal verification. If Eurydice compiled DynamicallySized to use a flexible array member everywhere, analysis of the C code might point out "missing" bounds checks that were not required in Rust. Conversely, if Eurydice added extra bounds checks, it would need to manufacture extra error paths that don't appear in the Rust source and that should be completely unused.

So, Eurydice emits two different types: a version of the dynamically sized type that has a flexible array member, and one that has a known-length array member. Converting between the two representations is a no-op at run time, but it technically violates C's strict-aliasing rule. Therefore Protzenko recommends compiling Eurydice-generated code with -fno-strict-aliasing .

This approach, of compiling a more abstract language to C in a way that preserves the structure of the code, is not new. The KaRaMeL project, upon which Eurydice is based, does the same thing for the F* programming language. F* is a dependently typed functional programming language used to develop cryptographic libraries. Compiling provably correct F* programs to equivalent C lets those libraries be used in programs where performance is a concern.

Unfortunately, Eurydice doesn't currently scale much beyond small examples. Rather than implement its own parser and typechecker for Rust code, Eurydice uses another Aeneas tool — Charon — to extract the parsed and preprocessed program from rustc. When I tested Charon on a variety of Rust packages, it was routinely foiled by more recent Rust features such as const generics .

When Charon does work, however, it dumps rustc's medium-level intermediate representation (MIR) as JSON, along with any compiler flags necessary to understand the compilation. Eurydice reads this JSON representation and converts it to KaRaMeL's intermediate representation. Then it uses a series of small passes over the KaRaMeL code to eliminate some Rust-specific details, before handing things over to the same code-generation logic that KaRaMeL uses for F*.

In its current form, Eurydice works best for small, self-contained programs that avoid complex Rust features. Within that niche, however, it works well. The generated code maintains the same structure as the original Rust code, except for places where Eurydice emits extra intermediate variables or needs some glue code to implement a more complicated feature. On the other hand, small self-contained code is also the easiest to rewrite by hand, so bringing in Eurydice is probably only worthwhile if the original Rust code is going to be updated and one wants an automatic solution to keep them in sync. In any case, Eurydice is only the newest tool in a rapidly expanding collection of ways to fold, spindle, and mutilate Rust code to fit into more environments.

items.title: 'Everyone hates the police' – what France's school protests reveal about a divided nation
items.summary: Students taking to the streets in France have become a focal point in the country's increasingly polarised politics.
items.content:
As dustbins burn and students chant "everyone hates the police" in the French city of Lille, one teenager explains why he and his friends have taken to the streets.

"There aren't even enough chairs. We have to go and find some at the start of every lesson," the 16-year-old, who did not want to give his name, says of his school.

"We've got 50 minutes to eat at lunchtime but there are 2,000 of us that need to get through the canteen."

He is one of hundreds of thousands of students who have protested across France since the end of last month over staff shortages and dilapidated facilities in the country's lycées, secondary schools attended by 15 to 18-year-olds.

Despite the government's apparent attempts to make concessions, the students show no sign of backing down.

"They have armies, they have the police, they have the powers," says Massicella, 18, as she marches through Lille. "But we have the mass population."

The protests, which have turned violent, have become a focal point in France's polarised politics, with all sides accusing the other of escalating tensions. As a presidential election approaches, politicians on both the hard right and hard left have sought to capitalise on the unrest and on what many see as the government's inability to resolve the crisis.

The protests - ignited at the Lycée Antoine-de-Saint-Exupéry in the deprived Paris suburb of Créteil - have struck a chord across the country.

Videos of rats scuttling through corridors in other lycées soon hit social media, providing striking symbols of the discontent. Other videos on TikTok and Instagram showed broken toilets, holes in walls and mouldy ceilings across the country. Students have complained of unbearable heat in the summer and freezing classrooms in the winter.

The anger has also focused on long school hours, chronic staff shortages, overcrowded classes and a deeply unpopular university admissions system.

The problem for the French government - which became clearer as we spoke to dozens of pupils this week - is that even if a tiny minority of schools have a problem with rodents, a very large number of pupils believe their own education is failing them.

On Tuesday, the government said 250,000 people marched, most of them young. The trade unions said it was more like half a million.

But it is not just students taking to the streets - their teachers are joining them.

Secondary school teacher Marine Monins, who joined the demonstrations in Lille, shows us a laminated timetable which she says illustrates the problem.

It has become normal for pupils to start at 8am and finish as late as 6pm, but the days are punctuated by hours-long gaps because of bad planning and staff shortages.

When lessons do go ahead, the classes are typically packed with 35 pupils (by comparison, the average secondary school class in England has fewer than 23 pupils).

"It's now impossible to give every child the attention they deserve," Monins explains.

On Thursday, the French government made its first sign of ceding ground to protesters, with a promise of 3,000 extra supply teachers in the coming days.

Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said by the end of October there will be a plan unveiled to respond to the crisis. Ministers have said they could look again at resources for schools within next year's squeezed budget.

But this has been met with a collective shrug at barricaded school gates across the country.

"It goes beyond having decent toilets in schools," lycée student Alcidor says in Paris, under the statue of Marianne at Place de la République, a place synonymous with protest.

"It's strong anger from the youth in France that doesn't feel represented, that feels abandoned, that feels unheard and is scared of what's coming in the future."

So far, almost 7,000 people have been detained during the disorder with more than 85% being children, according to the interior ministry.

More than 700 police officers have been injured in the past three weeks.

But rights groups and unions accuse the police of resorting to heavy-handed tactics against minors, including the use of batons, tear gas and non-lethal flash-ball guns. At least 200 pupils have been injured, along with dozens of teachers.

A 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a confrontation between police and demonstrators in the northern city of Lens.

Reports of how the teenager sustained the injury differ. A police union source cited by the AFP news agency said the boy appeared to have picked up a sting-ball grenade fired by riot police, which then exploded in his hand. However, a witness told local media that the teenager did not pick up the grenade.

A teacher at the boy's school, Bastien Riez, who is also a union rep, believes that current police tactics could irrevocably damage the relationship with France's youth.

"For many, this is their first experience of democracy and protest, and they are met with police and a sham of social dialogue and democracy. I fear that many young people will stop believing in this so-called democracy altogether."

Police have since been banned from using stun grenades at school protests.

But Parisian pupil Kaspar, 15, speaks of his fear when coming face-to-face with police in full riot gear. He says he and his friends have been protesting peacefully, but strangers were hijacking their protests.

"These people are coming just to shoot fireworks at police officers and they run. This is not the message we want to send to the world."

Police chiefs say violence, directed by agitators who have no link to the schools, is making their job incredibly hard.

Michel Chaballier, deputy secretary-general of the National Police Commissioners' Union (SCPN), says he fears the "political climate has been radicalised", and it was more and more difficult to have a calm, constructive public debate ahead of the national vote next spring.

"Police officers find themselves caught in the middle of this social tension, which is sometimes fuelled by irresponsible politicians," he says. "That's a shame, because I think this country deserves better."

The protests have become another bruising battleground in France's culture wars, with leaders of the hard left and right seeking to capitalise.

More than three-quarters of under-30s in France interviewed for an Ipsos survey conducted for Aix-Marseille University this week said they were worried about the state of their country.

But many people have a more profound and wider concern about just how dramatically the middle ground in France is eroding, leaving a chasm in the political landscape.

The education crisis is symptomatic of this but also threatens to act as an accelerant.

Most polling suggests more and more French citizens are looking to political extremes for answers to their problems – whether they are linked to education, the economy, identity or immigration.

Marine Le Pen of the hard right National Rally is the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race.

Next, neck and neck, are Édouard Philippe and Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

Philippe was a prime minister in President Emmanuel Macron's first term and has since founded a centre-right party called Horizons.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a veteran hard-left politician and founder of France Unbowed (LFI), has been a prominent older face among the students at rallies over the past three weeks.

Opponents have accused him of provoking and profiting from the unrest, while he counters that only his party truly represents the French youth.

He claims the current movement that has emerged from the schools protest is the most potent since 1968, when huge demonstrations almost brought down the government of President Charles de Gaulle. At its height, 10 million workers were on the streets before fresh elections led to the revolt fizzling out, but not before carving an indelible memory in French social history.

Despite being born more than four decades later, an exasperated generation of French teenagers are looking to the past for inspiration.

"I personally want to reproduce 1968!" Massicella declares in Lille, as she nears the end of the protest march.

Le Pen has stayed away from the protests and her most notable interventions have come in condemning the damage to schools, which is said to run into the millions of euros.

She has also suggested that parents of children who have committed the vandalism should pay for repairs.

The principle of casseur-payeur – those who break have to pay – has been an impassioned topic that has dominated French media this week.

The problem for President Macron is that there is no quick fix.

This is not a scenario where there is an unpopular piece of legislation that can be withdrawn in a hasty reverse ferret the prime minister is tasked with performing. That was the case with the gilets jaunes – the relentless protest in high vis jackets over a fuel tax rise nearly a decade ago.

Wholesale reform of the education system would cost billions – in new classrooms, new facilities, new teachers – and take years to achieve.

And changes that may seem more easily done – such as a reduction of the length of the school day – would be hugely problematic to implement logistically.

items.title: Rewriting Prime Agent in Rust
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.primeintellect.ai/blog/prime-agent-rust Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027694 Points: 39 # Comments: 13
items.content:
Since we launched Prime Agent [1] in August, it has been downloaded more than 300,000 times and has processed over 8 trillion tokens. Today, we're excited to ship a faster, cleaner and more reliable Prime Agent, rewritten from the ground up in Rust.

Over two weeks, Prime Agent orchestrated a swarm of over 2,000 agents to rewrite itself end to end, operating across 10,000+ Prime Sandboxes with over 200 billion tokens from Prime Inference’s GLM-5.3 endpoint. The Rust rewrite stress-tested Prime Agent’s multi-agent capabilities, including the sandbox and inference infrastructure we’ve been building to power large-scale agent swarms, autonomous research, and reinforcement learning.

To ensure feature parity with the TypeScript version, Prime Agent orchestrated subagents to topologically sort dependencies, with finite state machines structuring looped computations and correctness checks. In parallel, we rewrote the code architecture for easier maintenance and development. We then used runtime benchmarks and real Prime Agent traces to hillclimb performance metrics and triage bugs. Now, Prime Agent runs faster and uses fewer resources than most coding agent harnesses.

TypeScript helped us ship Prime Agent quickly, but its types are optional and disappear at runtime, errors travel as unchecked exceptions, CPU-heavy work like rendering and parsing large sessions competes with keyboard input on a single event loop, and every process pays for a JavaScript runtime and garbage collector. We want to keep shipping as fast as we do, while holding the code to a higher standard as it grows, and Rust suits that well:

In addition to these clear performance gains, the rewrite gives us the opportunity to rethink our design choices. We have significantly modularized our codebase, and are reaping the rewards of this rewrite, including Windows support, session crash isolation, and a more consistent daemon protocol.

Our goal was for agents to perform the rewrite autonomously with as little human intervention as possible. Thus, the human work required was to setup proper verification to enable autonomous deployment at scale. We followed similar setup to previous work on automatic Rust translation [2] . Each specification covered a different kind of parity:

With an objective check for every kind of parity, the agents could measure their own progress and catch regressions before changes merged, which let us cut back on human review. Remaining bugs and behavior differences were largely found through internal use, which guided our follow-up work on missing features, reliability and interface polish.

We ran all orchestrators and their agents on two 8-core on-demand CPU nodes, each supporting over 100 concurrent subagents and their respective CPython kernels. Additionally, since compilation, type-checking and diffing would saturate any single machine when dozens of agents are running at once, we built out utilities for our agents to outsource heavy work to Prime Sandboxes, allowing us to heavily parallelize our port.

A single root agent orchestrated the rewrite and divided the work into a topological ordering of tasks. The root agent wrote no product code, keeping it free to monitor every task, merge finished work, and maintain an overview of the rewrite while working with us on priorities and decisions. We also kept generation and verification in separate agents, since an agent that writes code is biased when evaluating it. Therefore, each task assigned by the orchestrator moved through four agents:

A failed review or verification sends the feature back to the implementer with the findings, and the PR merges once both pass. We are building this pattern into Prime Agent to orchestrate a factory of finite state machines, so workflows like this one can be defined once, reused, and updated.

Porting to Rust also gave us a chance to restructure the codebase. This is where much of the long-term benefit comes from:

While the autonomous workflow went further than we expected, the parity checks only verified the behavior they exercised. Once parity on the main RLM loop was achieved, we moved all our rewrite agents onto Rust, allowing us to dogfood the Rust version at scale (and now Prime Agent Rust was recursively improving itself!). Later, we moved our internal team onto the Rust build for daily use, which exposed bugs and missing behavior outside the coverage of the differential tests. Throughout our dogfood cycles, we had agents review logs and traces from all beta users, allowing us to automatically diagnose and resolve runtime and agent issues identified by users. We also took the rewrite as an opportunity to redesign some of the UX/TUI flows and model-facing API.

Bringing the rewrite to release quality took follow-up work over the following weeks, from finishing feature ports and fixing bugs to improving performance and polishing the interface. Prime Agent still wrote and tested these changes, while we had humans in the loop involved in finding problems, directing the changes, and reviewing all results.

With feature parity achieved, we wanted to optimize Prime Agent runtime performance across all user flows. We approached it the same way as the rewrite: by giving the agents an objective way to measure their own progress. We built a benchmark harness that measures Prime Agent performance across a variety of runtime metrics, and let Prime Agent hillclimb its speed and resource usage with well-deliberated improvements.

The performance benchmark evaluates Prime Agent in Rust and TypeScript, as well as other agent harnesses, on a fresh 4-core, 8 GB Prime Sandbox per benchmark, with noise checks that withhold any result too unstable to compare. Agents run in a real terminal driven through a screen emulator against a scripted model, so timings reflect what a user sees and exclude inference.

With the harness in place, a second orchestrator ran a hillclimbing loop for three days with a single objective: improve the benchmark results without breaking parity. Each experiment followed the same procedure:

We deliberately gave the loop no numeric targets, since a fixed threshold tends to become a stopping point. The agents' only objective was to keep improving the benchmarks without breaking parity for as long as measurable gains remained. Over the hillclimb cycle, the loop logged over 144 experiment and audit records, merging over 69 valid changes that boosted performance. Below are some significant improvements we’ve seen in important areas:

Most of the gains came from three kinds of change: moving work off the startup and render paths, replacing polling loops with event-driven waits, and releasing memory as soon as large sessions finished loading.

Overall, our Rust rewrite and following performance hillclimbing has made Prime Agent significantly faster and more resource efficient. With time to input roughly 14x faster than TypeScript and using over 80% less memory after startup, Prime Agent is amongst the fastest coding agent harnesses available.

External harness results were measured with our custom runtime suite. Without a common benchmark standard, comparisons should be interpreted with caution.

This more modular codebase and stronger compile-time checks will also help us ship new capabilities faster and catch more mistakes before they reach users.

With our Rust port in, we’re bringing the same attention to detail to every part of Prime Agent, from everyday systems interactions to complex work cross many agents. Now that infrastructural improvements are out of the way, we are accelerating on capabilities and evals, and making the multi-agent workflows behind this rewrite available to you.

Prime Agent will also be more tightly knit into the Prime Intellect ecosystem, allowing you to work across the stack with cloud agent swarms, inference, traces, sandboxes, evals, hosted training, and more.

With this rewrite, we are also releasing Prime Agent with native Windows support (beta) and installation through homebrew. Prime Agent remains open source and installs with one command:

items.title: Meloni si smarca. La scelta anti-tycoonper non perdere voti
items.summary: Ma Palazzo Chigi eviterà di cavalcare la difesa della Corte e proverà a giocare la carta della soluzione diplomatica
items.content:
ROMA – La riflessione, a Palazzo Chigi, è stata breve. Il confronto con la Farnesina ancora più rapido. Impossibile per l’Italia non partecipare alla dichiarazione congiunta con cui i membri del G7 (ad eccezione degli Stati Uniti) si sono schierati a favore della Corte penale internazionale e contro le sanzioni annunciate da Donald Trump. Impossibile restare al fianco di Washington – in questa battaglia spalleggiata da Israele – senza pagare un prezzo politico devastante. Un costo che la premier non intende affrontare, a pochi mesi dalle elezioni.

Non c’è stato dubbio, dunque. Per non rischiare di finire nel mirino delle opposizioni, fonti della Farnesina anticipano la pubblicazione dello statement e fanno sapere che Roma ha aderito alla condanna: meglio non tacere, perché potrebbe passare il messaggio che l’Italia si voglia schierare soltanto a causa delle critiche del centrosinistra. E così si spiega anche l’intervento di Antonio Tajani: «Il Nobel per la Pace è assegnato. È stata scelta una donna che ha una grande esperienza, è giusto che sia così. Non è che gli Usa devono commentare a chi si dà il premio».

Gli alleati europei erano stati preallertati dagli americani della mossa ostile alla Cpi. E avevano subito ragionato di come reagire. Prima della riunione dei ministri degli Esteri che licenzia il testo congiunto, Tajani ottiene l’ultimo via libera da Meloni. Inevitabile. E neanche particolarmente rischioso: lo scudo fornito dalle capitali europee e dagli altri partner del G7 rende la presa di posizione neanche troppo scomoda o scivolosa.

Arriva proprio nelle ore in cui Trump si presenta al Columbus day per ammiccare all’elettorato italo-americano con l’obiettivo di convincerlo a sostenerlo nelle elezioni di medio termine. Ma è una partita diversa, casi distinti che corrono su altri binari. E comunque, Palazzo Chigi eviterà di cavalcare la difesa della Cpi, a differenza di altri partner, anche perché con la Corte le relazioni restano fredde dopo il caso Al Masri. Semmai l’esecutivo batterà sulla necessità di provare a ricucire nel corso dei sei mesi che i contendenti hanno deciso di far trascorrere prima che le sanzioni entrino effettivamente in vigore .

La lettura di quanto accaduto tra Trump e la Cpi, invece, è univoca nelle diverse cancellerie continentali e occidentali. Ed è la stessa fornita informalmente dall’esecutivo italiano: una mossa ispirata da Benjamin Netanyahu, una sponda offerta dal tycoon all’amico in difficoltà in vista delle politiche in Israele.

Altre elezioni, quelle che in Italia si terranno nel 2027, orientano le mosse di Palazzo Chigi. Da molti mesi ormai – e certamente dopo gli insulti pubblici ricevuti da Trump – la presidente del Consiglio evita di mettere troppo la faccia sulle decisioni del Presidente Usa. Di difenderlo, di sostenerlo. Ha pagato un prezzo con l’opinione pubblica, non intende replicare. Certo, cerca di ripristinare relazioni civili. Ma per aiutarlo non intende rompere il fronte europeo, e men che meno mostrarsi conciliante con “Bibi”: non conviene e fa perdere voti, è la lezione ormai chiara al vertice del governo.

items.title: Atari Falcon
items.summary: Article URL: https://atarimuseum.nl/atari-falcon/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027590 Points: 35 # Comments: 10
items.content:
The Atari Falcon030 Computer System was Atari Corporation’s final computer product. Codenamed Sparrow, the machine was based on a Motorola 68030 main CPU, and had a Motorola 56000 digital signal processor, a feature which distinguished it from most other microcomputers of the era.

The Falcon was released in late 1992 and subsequently cancelled in late 1993 as Atari Corp restructured itself to focus completely on the release and support of its newest product, the Atari Jaguar video game console.

Atari Corp. created a number of prototypes of the Falcon040 (based on the more capable fully pipelined, integrated-FPU, Motorola 68040, and using a “microbox” case), but canceled it. The microbox case resembled the later Sony PlayStation 2, right down to the ability to run it vertically or horizontally. It is even referenced in the PS2 patent applications.

Shortly after release Atari Corp. bundled the MultiTOS Operating system in addition to TOS. TOS remained in ROM, and MultiTOS was supplied on floppy disk and could be installed to boot from hard disk.

In 1995, the music company C-Lab bought the rights to the Falcon hardware design and began producing their own versions. The Falcon Mk I was a direct continuation of Atari Corp.’s Falcon030 with TOS 4.04. The Falcon Mk II addressed a number of shortcomings in the original design, making it more suitable to use in a recording studio (these were unofficially termed ‘Cubase modifications’) such as accepting Line-level audio in without the need for a pre-amp or mixer.

Today, the Falcon is one of Atari Corp.’s most popular machines for hardware modding. Due to its expansion capabilities, several accelerators have been produced. Some of them overclock the CPU and/or the bus, while others upgrade the CPU to a Motorola 68060.

This is the collection of original hardware and software. None of this collection is for sale. If you have an item which is not on the list, please contact me and maybe we can trade. Donations are welcome too 🙂

A big Thank You! to Serge van Keulen for giving me the opportunity to add a lot of 16-bit items to the collection, including this Falcon!

items.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
items.summary: The conservative commentator currently works as a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group.
items.content:
Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the US president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokeswoman at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Trump called Zacharia "loyal" and "a devoted fan and member of MAGA" in a social media post on Friday, referring to his Make America Great Again movement, adding that she had "an unblemished record of support".

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

"She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7," Trump wrote on Truth Social of Zacharia.

"I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration."

Zacharia thanked him in a post on X, writing: "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime."

She said Trump had "shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day".

She said she looked forward "to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out".

The 42-year-old political strategist is a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News, and has been active in Republican politics for most of her adult life, having worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and for the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

Since June, she has been a senior communications adviser for Trump's media company and Truth Social platform, according to her LinkedIn profile. She worked in Homeland Security from February to March this year.

While she was only briefly in government at DHS - which the mother of four later said she left because of the strain of travel between California and Washington on her family - she has long been a ferocious defender of President Trump and his administration's policies.

In a June interview with the BBC , for example, she dismissed criticism of Trump's controversial use of the White House to host a televised UFC fight, saying the principles of the UFC "are the kind of principles that founded our Constitutional Republic".

"It's about not giving up the fight until the bitter end," she said. "I think there's no better summation of the American ethos than a good UFC fight."

Earlier this year, Zacharia wrote an op-ed in the New York Post about an incident in which she was asked to stop wearing a "Make America Great Again" hat to her local gym.

"I responded that I would never take my Trump hat off to appease the left," she wrote. "This is raw, unfiltered intolerance. Freedom of speech doesn't evaporate at the gym door."

Justin Buchler, a political science professor at Case Western Reserve University in Ohio, told the BBC that Trump's appointments during his second term have been "based on personal affiliation and loyalty".

"He values loyalty first and foremost," Buchler told the BBC.

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

In 2011, she spent nearly two years clerking at a law firm in Beijing, China.

Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

The complex job of press secretary goes beyond the briefing room podium to include managing contentious relationships with the press, coordinating with other parts of the White House, and providing media advice to the president. The secretary also oversees an office that receives a significant amount of inquiries and requests on a daily basis.

Yanna Krupnikov, a political scientist and professor of communication and media at the University of Michigan, said the selection of Zacharia "speaks to a blurring of the lines between different media types".

Politicians nowadays need to communicate not only to various news outlets but with people in a social media context, she said.

"I think the goal is not as much speaking to the media and journalists, but making sure that particular, very specific sound-bytes and messages get to ordinary people," Krupnikov told the BBC.

When Leavitt left the role, Trump called her one of his "most trusted aides", which sets a high bar for her replacement. Leavitt left because she said she wanted to spend more time with her family.

items.title: Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices
items.summary: The US president hopes to ease his party's pain before next month's midterm elections, writes the BBC's North America correspondent.
items.content:
Donald Trump's decision to import Russian fuel to the US represents a remarkable about-face from the president.

Just three weeks ago, Trump signed legislation to authorise fresh American sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas.

Now, Trump says, Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to supply hundreds of thousands of tons of diesel fuel to the US and world markets in the coming months.

The deal comes as Trump is still grappling with the political fallout of the Iran war and its impact on global energy prices, weeks before American voters head to the polls in the midterm elections.

As the cost of fuel has skyrocketed in America, his standing with the public – stung by the higher prices at the pump and knock-on effects that led to across-the board inflation – has soured.

The toll the war is taking has been acutely felt by US agricultural states, which rely heavily on diesel to operate farming machinery and to transport their products to market.

It is these states – places like Iowa, Kansas, Texas and Ohio – that have become unexpected political battlegrounds in the upcoming elections that will determine if Republicans maintain control of Congress.

Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'

For months, the American president has been searching for ways to ease his party's political pain.

He recently pressured European allies to further tap their oil reserves . He deferred federal taxes on the fuel and authorised supplies designated for farm use to be used in interstate trucking.

He has also promised that he would not renew attacks on Iran until after the midterms – an unusually frank acknowledgement of the political impact the ongoing conflict is having.

His decision to strike a deal with Russia's Putin is only the latest, most dramatic effort.

Trump's Truth Social posts often provide incomplete information, of course. The details of exactly how Russia is supplying this fuel to the global market, and what they might get for in return – besides much-needed hard currency – is unclear.

It opens Trump to criticism from European allies and American politicians that his administration is now helping to fund the Russian war machine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the deal a "gift" to Putin that Russia would "repay" with "terror and perfidy".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on X.

It is also uncertain exactly how much Trump's move will help Republicans at the ballot box.

The promised European diesel release hasn't moved energy prices significantly, and there's no information on the speed with which Russian fuel could enter the market.

Its diesel refinery capacity has been damaged by repeated Ukrainian strikes – attacks that Trump has encouraged Zelensky to curtail.

The US uses approximately 3.6 million barrels of diesel a day, so even if Russia delivers its promised 300,000 tons this month, that amounts to approximately half of the US daily consumption.

With less than a month before November's midterm elections, early voting has already started in many states. The political cake, as the saying goes, is all but baked.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in his Truth Social post.

But over the past seven months, prices on energy, fuel and consumer goods have only gone up - even as Trump and his officials have repeatedly assured an uneasy public a successful resolution to the war, and an easing of its economic impact, is nearly at hand.

Trump may be left hoping that his latest deal, setting aside its potentially uncomfortable diplomatic issues, will be enough to convince American voters that his promise of impending economic relief is more than just empty words.

Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?

items.title: Terremoto di magnitudo 7.6 a Panama, gli Usa escludono il rischio tsunami
items.summary: Sospesa l'attività dell'aeroporto, chiuse le scuole. Scene di panico nella capitale. Al momento non si hanno notizie di vittime. Seconda scossa di magnitudo 6
items.content:
Un terremoto di magnitudo 7.6 è stato registrato nel sud di Panama , a 14 chilometri a sudovest di Pitaloza Arriba. Lo riporta l'istituto geologico statunitense Usgs. Il forte sisma ha provocato il panico nella capitale Panama City, riferiscono giornalisti Afp. Poco dopo c 'è stata una seconda scossa di terremoto di magnitudo 6. Lo comunica la rete panamense Rpc tv che sta già inviando le prime immagini di palazzi incrinati e calcinacci per strada, gente per strada dopo il forte terremoto che ha colpito lo stato centramericano. Al momento non si hanno notizie di vittime.

Le autorità stanno invitando la popolazione a non intasare le linee telefoniche e lasciare spazio ai soccorsi.

"Ho richiesto un rapporto ai ministri e agli enti competenti in merito agli effetti: si invita alla calma. Non c'è motivo di usare l'accaduto per generare allarme e disordine". Lo ha scritto su X il presidente di Panama Josè Mulino subito dopo il terremoto.

L'aeroporto internazionale di Panama h a comunicato di aver sospeso le attività per motivi precauzionali e per poter controllare le strutture. Inoltre sono state chiuse le scuole . Nelle zone più colpite di Coclè, Verguas e Azuero i vigili del fuoco stanno cominciando a verificare la tenuta degli edifici. I media locali trasmettono scene di persone che scappano nel panico dalle loro case e dai centri commerciali evacuati, dopo le scosse.

Il sistema di monitoraggio tsunami degli Stati Uniti ha diramato un'allerta per potenziale minaccia tsunami per diversi Paesi che si affacciano sul Pacifico orientale, dopo il sisma che ha colpito Panama. La segnalazione di possibile minaccia riguarda Ecuador, Colombia, Nicaragua, Panama, Guatemala, Messico, Perù, El Salvador, Costa Rica.

Lo 'U.S. Tsunami Warning System' ha poi ritirato l'allerta tsunami sulle coste centroamericane del Pacifico dopo aver pubblicato un primo avvertimento a seguito del terremoto di magnitudo 7,6. U na minaccia moderata di tsunami viene considerata invece dalle autorità di El Salvador mentre il rischio dell'arrivo di un'onda anomala viene scartato dall'Unità nazionale del rischio disastri della Colombia (Ungrd).

Trump sospende le sanzioni sul diesel russo: subito agli Usa e al mondo 300mila tonnellate e 2 milioni entro l’anno. Ringrazia Putin: "I prezzi scenderanno rapidamente e a livelli record". Il Cremlino conferma: "Forniremo petrolio agli Usa e al mondo". Zelensky: “Regalo orribile e disonesto, non porta la pace”. La Ue per ora tace.

AXios: Witkoff e Kushner valutano viaggio a Mosca e Kiev la prossima settimana

Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner stanno considerando di andare a Mosca e a Kiev la prossima settimana per parlare di proposta di pace. Lo riporta Axios citando alcune fonti, secondo le quali non è chiaro come le tensioni sull'accordo con la Russia per il diesel possano influenzare le loro decisioni.

“Trump si è accordato con Putin dopo che Zelensky ha ignorato le sue richieste”

Donald Trump ha deciso di concludere l'accordo con la Russia sul diesel dopo che Volodymyr Zelesnky ha ignorato le ripetute richieste americane di fermare gli attacchi alle raffinerie di petrolio russe. Lo riporta Axios citando alcune fonti. "Zelensky sta valutando male la situazione. Continuando a colpire le raffinerie, sta compromettendo" la fiducia e la la disponibilità ottenuta da Trump negli ultimi sei mesi, ha spiegato un funzionario americano. Il presidente voleva che l'Ucraina fermasse unilateralmente gli attacchi alle raffinerie perché stavano facendo salire i prezzi dell'energia negli Stati Uniti.

Durante le otto ore di colloqui ieri a Miami con i negoziatori ucraini, Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner li avevano avvertiti della telefonata fra Trump e Putin e della rimozione delle sanzioni sul diesel russo perché Kiev aveva ignorato le seu richieste. Secondo una fonte ucraina, gli inviati di Trump hanno minacciato anche si togliere all'Ucraina l'intelligence necessaria per agire se continuerà a ignorare le richieste del presidente. Gli americani però smentiscono la ricostruzione e mettono in evidenza che Witkoff e Kushner hanno solo spiegato che gli attacchi stavano causando problemi negli Stati Uniti. Fino all'accordo con la Russia, le trattative a Miami erano andate bene. Si erano concentrate sulle garanzie di sicurezza ed erano state presentate nuove proposte per soluzioni territoriali.

Witkoff: “Oggi le trattative con Ue, Kiev e Nato sono state costruttive”

Le trattative fra gli "Stati Uniti, l'E3, la commissione europea, l'Ucraina e la Nato sono state costruttive". Lo afferma l'inviato speciale Steve Witkoff, sottolineando che sono state discusse "potenziali strade per una de-escalation e per la fine della guerra con la Russia prima dell'inverno e gli sforzi per una pace duratura". I colloqui hanno riguardato un'ampia gamma di temi, "incluse misure di breve termine e le garanzie di sicurezza e anche accordi di lungo termine per la sicurezza dell'Ucraina ed Europea per prevenire futuri conflitti, sostenere la ricostruzione dell'Ucraina, incluso il suo accesso nell'Ue". Le parti hanno "affermato il loro impegno a una pace sostenibile che rafforzi la sicurezza e crei opportunità per una stabilità di lungo termine", ha messo in evidenza.

items.title: Anthropic AI model submits false tip on unsolved Philly murder
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/local/anthropic-ai-model-submits-false-tip-on-unsolved-philly-murder-police-say/4477051/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50027118 Points: 124 # Comments: 97
items.content:
An artificial intelligence (AI) model submitted a false tip on an unsolved Philadelphia murder, police said.

The false homicide tip was posted on PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com back on July 18, 2026, at 11:27 p.m., police said.

Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.

The AI company Anthropic said its model was conducting a test involving interactions with randomly selected websites when it accessed PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com and submitted false information on an unsolved homicide. The tip claimed to come from someone with information on the case.

Anthropic said they discovered the incident on Sept. 28 and terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission. The company also said they instituted an additional validation mechanism for future testing.

Anthropic notified Philadelphia police of the incident on Wednesday Oct. 7, and the department met with the company’s representatives on Thursday, Oct. 8., officials said. Police then located the submission in the website’s tip records and confirmed the corresponding email remained in spam.

“The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” a Philadelphia Police spokesperson wrote. “Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess - not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence. An automated submission does not bypass that process.”

Anthropic told police they will publish a report of the incident and other instances of unintended AI model behavior for the department’s review on Friday.

Breaking news and the stories that matter to your neighborhood.

“Those PPD safeguards limited the impact of this incident. They do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide,” the police spokesperson wrote. “Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers. Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement.”

Philadelphia police, the city’s Law Department, Office of Innovation and Technology and Mayor Cherelle Parker’s executive team continue to investigate the incident.

“The City of Philadelphia takes this incident very seriously. The company must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city’s knowledge,” the police spokesperson wrote. “The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable.”

Police encourage the public to continue to submit legitimate information about unsolved homicides through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com. They also said the Parker administration will closely monitor the incident and provide more information when it becomes available.

“In addition to our investigation into this incident, the Parker administration will explore all necessary regulatory protections going forward locally along with our state and federal partners,” the police spokesperson wrote. “The City of Philadelphia under Mayor Parker’s leadership is adopting AI responsibly, and is committed to transparency, careful implementation, and safeguards that reduce errors and protect City systems and residents.”

NBC10 reached out to Anthropic for comment. We will include a statement once we receive one.

items.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
items.summary: The planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.
items.content:
US Vice-President JD Vance has cast doubt on the Pentagon's plans to livestream a firing squad execution of the Fort Hood attacker.

Vance expressed uncertainty to reporters about whether the December execution would go ahead as planned, saying: "I don't know that that's actually going to happen". He added, that "if it's through live stream, I'm not going to be watching it".

Hours later, President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved the live stream plans but the Pentagon was still "making a determination" on it.

Nidal Hasan killed 13 unarmed soldiers at a base in Texas in 2009, injuring another 32. The firing squad execution would be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

The Pentagon announced earlier this week it would execute Nisan, a former US Army major, on 3 December by firing squad in the attack on the Fort Hood base.

Then on Thursday US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be livestreamed for the public. "People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth explained.

Trump, as he left the White House on Friday, was asked about the possibility that visuals of Hasan's execution could be used as propaganda for terrorists.

"He killed 13, 14 people, badly wounded 20-some-odd people, and he's totally nuts," Trump said. "So I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes, and I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him."

The Pentagon declined to comment further when asked for more information about a decision on the livestream.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Vance condemned Hasan's attack on the base as "the worst terrorist attack on American soil outside of 9/11". Asked about how his Catholic faith impacted his stance on the plan to stream a public execution, Vance questioned whether it would happen.

But he noted that Hasan, who was a US Army psychiatrist, was meant to treat soldiers for mental illness and other problems and "took them at their most vulnerable and gunned down these people where they lived".

The announcement about a possible livestream has been met with criticism from both political parties.

Republican Senator John Curtis pointed to Rome's history of a "bloody spectacle" corrupting people who watched them, warning that public executions erode civilisations "when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment".

Curtis said that Hegseth's plan "risks feeding that appetite" and urged him to reconsider.

"The victims deserve justice administered with solemnity. Broadcasting a death diminishes us and is not an effective deterrent," he said.

Democratic Senator Chris Murphy told CNN that the idea was "disgusting" and reminiscent of executions carried out by the Islamic State group.

Georgia lawmaker Austin Scott, a Republican, said that he "absolutely" supports the death sentence, but that live-streaming executions "is what jihadists do. America is better than that".

John Bolton, a former national security adviser during the first Trump administration, told BBC's Radio 4 PM that he supports capital punishment, but that the livestream is "unnecessary" because there are provisions for interested parties to view the execution in person or to report on it.

"I just think this is a mark by Secretary Hegseth doing something he thinks will please President Trump. That's the way he's been running the defence department. I think that's really not appropriate for a secretary of defence," Bolton said.

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops condemned the decision to publicly livestream Hasan's execution, expressing "shock and great sorrow" in a statement.

The UN human rights office told AFP that livestreaming it would be "tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture".

Hasan opened fire in a crowded medical building where deploying soldiers were awaiting check-ups and vaccines.

He later admitted in court that he was the gunman and apologised for "any mistakes". He said during his court-martial in 2013 that he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military.

The killings on 5 November 2009 were the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American military base.

Military law requires that military execution be approved by the US president. It also requires appellate review, when a higher court inspects the decision and gives a final judgement on its legality to move forward.

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. Eleven public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan, according to Amnesty International.

Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream

When Hegseth told reporters on Thursday about plans to ensure the public can watch the execution, he did not specify where or how live video of the execution would be shown.

A Pentagon spokesperson on Friday reiterated to the BBC that Hasan's execution "will be livestreamed," but said the government had no further details "to provide at this time".

The White House did not respond to an inquiry about whether it expected to show Hasan's planned execution on its social media channels.

The White House maintains official accounts and channels on the most notable and widely used online platforms that are capable of streaming live video, namely Meta, YouTube, TikTok and X.

All of the platforms have prohibitions in place on violent images and videos, as well as those that show death or glorify or make a spectacle of violence.

Meta, owner of Instagram, Facebook and Threads, explicitly bans any live stream of capital punishment.

YouTube bans all "violent or gory content intended to shock or disgust viewers".

TikTok has a similar rule that bars "extremely graphic, violent, or disturbing content—especially when it could cause viewers emotional distress." That includes the "moment of someone's death" and "the shooting of an individual".

Both YouTube and TikTok make exceptions in instances of "public interest".

Asked if a live-stream of an execution qualifies for the exception if it is government-sanctioned , a TikTok spokeswoman said: "Regardless, I'd point you back to the not allowed section which reflects our approach."

The policy at X, which has loosened content moderation since billionaire Elon Musk took over the platform, prohibits content "glorifying" of violence. It will remove content depicting when a person dies will be removed if requested by certain parties.

Meta, YouTube and X did not respond to multiple BBC requests for comment on whether they would uphold their current policies in the event Hasan's execution is broadcast.

items.title: Powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake hits Panama, damaging buildings
items.summary: Tsunami warnings are issued for neighbouring countries as videos of destruction circulate online.
items.content:
A massive magnitude 7.7 earthquake has hit Panama, damaging buildings and causing widespread shaking.

About 4.6 million people felt moderate to severe tremors as a result of the quake, according to the US Geological Survey, which has said that the effects of the quake were "likely to be widespread".

It struck just before 15:00 local time (18:00 GMT) on Friday, with an epicentre about 6.2 miles (10km) from the town of Pitaloza Arriba in south-central Panama.

Footage shared online appears to show collapsed buildings in the towns of Penonomé and Soná, including one of a man calling out to anyone trapped under the rubble of a collapsed building. No casualties have so far been reported.

Verified footage shows one side of a cathedral in Penonomé collapsed due to the shaking, as well as one of its spires.

Another video showed a local hotel had almost completely collapsed.

Ricardo Brown, who lives in the southern Herrera province, told news agency Reuters that the earthquake had damaged several homes in his neighbourhood of Las Minas.

"We're scared. It's just the two of us old folks here. The house has cracked and we're afraid it could fall on us," the 74-year-old said.

The full extent of the damage it has caused is not yet clear, though several large aftershocks were also reported near the initial earthquake, potentially complicating the situation on the surface.

The quake was registered as occurring at a depth of just 12km. The shallower the earthquake, the more likely it is to have more severe effects on the surface.

Many people were evacuated from buildings in Panama City, about 200km from the epicentre, and were seen taking to the streets or sitting in nearby parks until the shaking had ceased.

Damage in the capital appears to be limited to that caused by debris falling from roofs.

Panama's President José Raúl Mulino said his entire government was mobilising in response to the earthquake, adding: "What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder."

Tsunami warnings were initially issued for 11 countries neighbouring Panama, before the US Tsunami Warning System confirmed there was no threat.

The Panama Canal - a vital waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans - was unaffected by the earthquake, the authority that oversees marine traffic through it said.

The earthquake comes just three days before Panama was scheduled to hold a national evacuation drill for dealing with a major earthquake.

It also follows devastating earthquakes in Colombia and Venezuela earlier this year.

items.title: Perù, Hitler Mussolini Simeón eletto sindaco a Queropalca
items.summary: Clamore mediatico per il nome del candidato vincitore
items.content:
Nelle recenti elezioni regionali e municipali in Perù, un candidato ha attirato l'attenzione generale per la particolarità del suo nome. Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores, esponente del partito Ahora Nación, è il vincitore virtuale per la carica di sindaco nel distretto di Queropalca, situato nella provincia di Lauricocha. La sua affermazione elettorale ha suscitato clamore mediatico per l'evidente coincidenza anagrafica con il leader del regime nazista e con il dittatore italiano fondatore del fascismo.

Il nuovo primo cittadino ha conquistato la vittoria ottenendo 229 preferenze, pari al 34,54% dei voti validi. La competizione elettorale distrettuale è stata serratissima e si è decisa per un margine minimo, con una differenza di appena 42 schede tra la prima e la terza posizione in classifica.

Al secondo posto si è infatti piazzato il partito Renovación Popular Perú con 204 voti (30,76%), seguito a stretto giro da País para Todos con 187 consensi. Molto più distaccati gli altri sfidanti, tra cui Alianza para el Progreso e Somos Perú (fermo a otto voti), in uno scrutinio che ha registrato un totale di 663 voti validi.

items.title: RTX Spark, modelli, prezzi e disponibilità in Italia. Per Surface Laptop Ultra ci sarà da attendere
items.summary: I primi notebook con NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X si possono già configurare e ordinare in Italia: per la nuova piattaforma NVIDIA si parte da poco più di 3.000 euro e si arriva a oltre 6.000, con la differenza di prezzo legata quasi esclusivamente alla memoria. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Sono aperti da meno di 24 ore i preordini dei primi laptop con piattaforma RTX Spark, e già arrivano le prime indicazioni: in Germania e in Francia, dove il Surface Laptop Ultra viene venduto, la versione da 128 GB di RAM è andata sold out in poche ore. Non possiamo ovviamente sapere di quanti laptop stiamo parlando, ma è evidente che da anni chi usa Windows aspettava una workstation con le caratteristiche promesse dal nuovo chip NVIDIA: consumi ridotti, piena potenza anche a batteria, fino a 128 GB di memoria unificata e prestazioni allineate a quelle della RTX 5070.

Il Surface Laptop Ultra in Italia al momento non arriva, e non escludiamo che la scelta possa essere legata proprio alla poca disponibilità di prodotto, ma MSI, Asus e Lenovo hanno aperto i preordini per i loro modelli, e la buona notizia è che si partirà da circa 3.000 euro, grazie a Lenovo, che offre una configurazione base molto allettante.

Lo Yoga Pro 9n Gen 11 da 15" parte infatti da 3.019,01 euro con N1X a 18 core (P-core fino a 3,90 GHz), 32 GB di LPDDR5X-9400 e 512 GB di storage. Se si vuole 1 TB di storage servono 90 euro in più.

Per avere più memoria bisogna passare alla versione da 20 core, con P-core fino a 4,00 GHz, che parte però da 4.839 euro con 64 GB di RAM e 1 TB di disco. Il disco da 2 TB costa 520 euro in più, si arriva a 5.339 euro. Stranamente basso il prezzo chiesto per passare alla versione da 128 GB: solo 300 euro, per un totale di 5.659 euro. È un prezzo alto, ma è anche il più basso in assoluto al quale si può trovare un RTX Spark con 128 GB di RAM.

Lenovo non ha solo il 15": c'è anche lo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 Gen 11 da 16", convertibile con OLED 2,8K (2.880 x 1.800) touch a 120 Hz e penna. Qui si parte da 3.619,01 euro per la versione con processore a 18 core, 32 GB di RAM e SSD da 512 GB. L'SSD da 1 TB costa qui 80 euro in più, mentre per il 20 core si passa a 4.759 euro, perché oltre al processore cambia anche la memoria, che sale a 64 GB. Il disco è da 1 TB, con 500 euro in più per il 2 TB. La memoria, invece, non si può espandere: questa macchina viene venduta solo nei tagli da 32 GB o da 64 GB.

MSI propone solo laptop con processore completo, quindi CPU a 20 core e GPU a 6.144 core. Il Prestige N16 Flip AI+, convertibile da 16" con batteria da 99,9 Wh e display Tandem OLED 3840 x 2400, parte da 4.299 euro per la versione da 64 GB con disco da 1 TB e arriva a 6.399 euro per quella da 128 GB con disco da 2 TB.

ASUS è l'unica a offrire RTX Spark in formato compatto, con il ProArt P14: 14" OLED 3K a 120 Hz, 1,48 kg e batteria da 90 Wh. I due modelli disponibili sono posizionati a 3.599 euro con 32 GB e a 5.599 euro con 128 GB, entrambi con la versione del processore più potente e con disco da 1 TB. C'è anche il modello da 16": 4.599 euro per 64 GB e 1 TB, 6.399 euro per il 128 GB con 2 TB.

Microsoft ha il bellissimo Surface Laptop Ultra, che possiamo considerare il reference design della piattaforma. In Italia non arriverà subito, ma possiamo prendere come riferimento i prezzi di Francia e Germania: 2.899 euro per RTX Spark in versione 18 core con GPU da 5.120 core, 24 GB e SSD da 512 GB; 3.399 euro per quella da 24 GB e 1 TB; 3.759 euro per 32 GB e 1 TB. La variante con processore completo, a 20 core e con GPU da 6.144 core, parte da 4.239 euro (32 GB, 1 TB), sale a 4.959 euro con 64 GB e a 5.439 euro con 2 TB, fino a 6.879 euro per la versione da 128 GB, che risulta, come abbiamo detto, già esaurita.

Al momento Dell e HP, gli altri due partner di NVIDIA per il lancio, non hanno annunciato la disponibilità per il nostro mercato.

items.title: Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet
items.summary: Thailand’s Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.
items.content:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province, southern Thailand, while King Maha Vajiralongkorn watched from the ground.

The Royal Household has said she is an experienced pilot, having logged about 1,188 hours across several types of aircraft since she began flying in 2010.

She also co-piloted aircraft carrying the King on official visits to other countries, the Royal Household said.

items.title: Il tribunale rigetta il ricorso di Ranucci per il reintegro a Report. Il giornalista: "Rispetto la sentenza e la accetto serenamente"
items.summary: L'ex conduttore: "Le mie battaglie compensate dall'affetto della gente"
items.content:
A 14 giorni dall'udienza, il tribunale del Lavoro di Roma ha rigettato il ricorso in via urgente presentato dal giornalista Sigfrido Ranucci con cui chiedeva il reintegro alla conduzione della trasmissione Report dopo la decisione della Rai del 28 agosto scorso con cui era stato rimosso. L'azienda aveva offerto al giornalista tre opzioni : la vicedirezione al Tg3 o a Rainews, oppure l'ufficio di corrispondenza dal Cairo. Proposte respinte al mittente dall'ex conduttore e che è passato alla via giudiziaria per ottenere il reintegro. "Che io rispetti la decsione è ovvio: mi sono sempre battuto per l'indipendenza della magistratura e battersi per un valore del genere non significa togliersi la maglietta quando non ti fa comodo per poi rimetterla all'occorrenza", il commento a caldo di Ranucci.

Nel provvedimento di oltre 30 pagine i giudici ripercorrono la vicenda, citando anche l'episodio dell'attentato subito da Ranucci nell'ottobre del 2025 e affermando che la decisione della Rai "di procedere ad una riorganizzazione della redazione, con avvicendamento autorale e di conduzione, appare, a un esame sommario, sganciata dalla parallela vicenda disciplinare e adottata quale mezzo di risoluzione della situazione di tensione interna creatasi tra i membri della redazione e, come tale, strumento di tutela del sereno operare di questa nel rispetto della normativa di legge". Nell'ordinanza i giudici richiamano anche le argomentazioni difensive portate in giudizio dall'azienda pubblica. Per la Rai "l'individuazione del conduttore, e del gruppo autorale, di un determinato programma televisivo" rientra "nelle prerogative dell'impresa editoriale ed è insindacabile. Pertanto, il giornalista non è titolare di un diritto soggettivo ad occupare una determinata posizione nell'ambito della programmazione televisiva". Entrando nel merito della questione il tribunale afferma che "si deve ritenere accertato, quanto meno in questa fase e tenuto conto dei tempi ristretti imposti da un'istruttoria necessariamente sommaria, che, a conferma delle motivazioni pur genericamente espresse nel provvedimento" della Rai del 28 agosto, "le vicende legate al caso dell'attentato che man mano emergevano dagli articoli di giornale ed il clamore che queste suscitavano sugli organi di stampa, avevano creato nell'ambito della redazione un clima di tensione che incideva sul proficuo operare della stessa, tanto che diversi redattori avevano sentito la necessità di manifestare tale disagio non solo al responsabile del programma Ranucci ma anche, per saltum, al superiore gerarchico di quest'ultimo". E ancora: "il malessere manifestato da più giornalisti membri della redazione è stato confermato, seppur con diversi accenti, dal medesimo dottor Ranucci, parimenti sentito in udienza, il quale ha sul punto dichiarato: 'Si erano lamentati con me, anzi avevano fatto presente la necessità di sopportare insieme la pressione mediatica e puntellare la mia posizione tramite una riorganizzazione. Sentivano la pressione mediatica e quindi mi avevano coinvolto essendo loro responsabile. Avevano bisogno di puntellare Report intorno la mia persona perché per 20 anni avevo garantito l'esistenza del programma'". Su eventuali pressioni politiche messe in atto per ottenere dalla Rai lo stop alla conduzione, il tribunale afferma "che l'accertata impropria pressione mediatica esercitata ad opera di esponenti di rilievo della maggioranza di Governo sulle decisioni aziendali, volta all'adozione di un provvedimento di rimozione di Ranucci, quale unico dato indiziario non corroborato da altri, non offra in sé, tenuto conto del quadro complessivo degli elementi acquisiti, prova sufficiente a far ritenere che si sia consumata effettiva e determinante interferenza ".

Per Ranucci, "è una decisione che ha abbracciato l'idea secondo cui il clamore mediatico può arrivare a far sostituire un conduttore con una redazione che ha subito delle pressioni e che, di conseguenza, non vi sia la prova che i dirigenti Rai abbiano subito un'influenza diretta da parte della politica", sottolinea a margine dell'evento "Censura di Stato - A sostegno di Report e del giornalismo d'inchiesta", organizzato da ANTIMAFIADuemila a Roma, dove viene accolto tra gli applausi. "Tutte le battaglie che ho fatto nella mia vita e che mi hanno portato a 247 querele, a una bomba, a essere sospeso e a subire la decurtazione dello stipendio, trovano compenso solo nell'affetto della gente. L'avete visto tutti: per me significa che ho fatto bene e questo mi basta", aggiunge Ranucci. I legali del giornalista prendono "atto della decisione che rispettiamo ma che non condividiamo. Valuteremo il provvedimento e le ulteriori iniziative da assumere nelle sedi competenti", affermano in una nota gli avvocati Franco Focareta, Franco Scarpelli, Stefano Rossi e Roberto De Vita. Soddisfatta la Rai: "È importante riconoscere il lavoro svolto dai vertici aziendali nel rispetto delle procedure e delle proprie responsabilità. L'auspicio è che questa decisione contribuisca a ristabilire un clima di serenità", commenta la consigliera di amministrazione Rai Federica Frangi.
